column1: # Shared oracle (#1023 C), measured with Java CaptureBoundaryParser.input(Kind.VALUE, ..) at the low-level
# Classic entry (snapshot 5043e336 + #1023 C owned fix). The boundary checks the source of the Parsed its
# child returns: a Choice, and a rule whose body is a Choice (Java LazyChoice), return the selected child's
# Parsed, so an input-backed child (`leaf`, `MO`) or a selected PEG assertion that returned no token (`!z`)
# is accepted in the virtual kinds too, although the virtual collector that kept nothing is generated "".
# Generated text (`gen*`) is rejected. Every row holds for Memoization x Diagnostics. Rust reads the same
# table with Expr::InputCaptureBoundary(capture_tree::Kind::Value, ..). Shapes are those of
# conformance/semantic-predicate-source and conformance/owned-capture-virtual, plus `gen0:g` and rules
# nested in rules: a body that is only a rule reference is a Java single-element LazyChain, so
# `Rule[Rule[Choice[..]]]` returns its own collection (generated "" in the virtual kinds) and is rejected
# there, while `Rule[Choice[Rule[Choice[leaf,z]],q]]` (LazyChoice of a LazyChoice) is accepted.
